reels.title: The Night the Mounds Open
reels.hook: On this night, the hills stood open

beats.text: Samhain. Old Irish Samain. The death of summer.
The Coligny calendar, Gaul, second century AD. First month: Samonios.
Irish scribes recorded what that night permitted.
The sídhe opened. The fairy mounds received the living.
In Echtra Nerai, a hanged corpse begs water from a living man.
Three weeks remain. The mound is already listening.

reels.caption: Samain marked the end of summer in Gaelic Ireland. The Gaulish Coligny calendar, inscribed in the second century AD, opens its year with the month Samonios. Irish literature fixed its terrors on this night — gates between worlds unlocked, the dead permitted passage. In Echtra Nerai, Nera carries a hanged man to drink, then follows a spectral host into the hill. Few return from that tale unchanged. Three weeks remain before the thirty-first. The full entry is in the Forbidden Library: alloccult.com

reels.title: The Jar at Nag Hammadi
reels.hook: He feared a jinn was inside

beats.text: Upper Egypt, December 1945. Muhammad Ali al-Samman digs for fertiliser.
His mattock strikes a sealed clay jar.
He hesitates. He fears what is inside.
No jinn. No gold. Leather-bound Coptic codices.
Fourth-century texts the Church had condemned. Buried sixteen centuries.
One opens: "These are the secret sayings…" Would you break the seal?

reels.caption: December 1945. A farmer near Nag Hammadi strikes a sealed jar. By his own account he feared a jinn. Inside: twelve codices and leaves of a thirteenth — Gnostic gospels buried for sixteen centuries. The Gospel of Thomas opens with secret sayings attributed to a living Jesus. The Church had condemned these words. The earth had kept them. Would you have broken the seal? Answer below. Read what was inside: alloccult.com

reels.title: The Beast Had a Name
reels.hook: The Beast's number was a man's name

beats.text: Revelation 13:18: "Let him that hath understanding count the number."
In Hebrew, every letter carries a number. Aleph: one. Tav: four hundred.
Spell Nero Caesar in Hebrew letters. נרון קסר. Count them.
Six hundred and sixty-six.
Some manuscripts read 616. Drop the final nun. The Latin spelling.
Abraxas in Greek totals 365. A god measured by the year.

reels.caption: Revelation hides its Beast inside arithmetic. Hebrew and Greek letters each carry numerical values. Nero Caesar, written in Hebrew as נרון קסר, totals 666. Drop one letter — the Latin spelling — and you reach 616. Some early manuscripts read exactly that. Abraxas, in Greek isopsephy, totals 365: a deity measured by the solar year. Save this. Comment any word and we will count it. The full table is at alloccult.com

reels.title: Case File I: Arnold Paole
reels.hook: Serbia, 1732. The army filed a vampire report

beats.text: Medveđa, Serbia. Former soldier Arnold Paole dies from a fall.
He had claimed a vampire tormented him in life.
He ate earth from its grave. He smeared himself with its blood.
Weeks after burial, four villagers die. They name Paole.
Exhumed after forty days: no decay. Fresh blood at the mouth.
Staked, he was said to groan. Case File II: next week.

reels.caption: Case File I. In 1732, Austrian army surgeon Johann Flückinger signed Visum et Repertum — a witnessed and reported account of the case of Arnold Paole of Medveđa. Paole had claimed a vampire attacked him in his Ottoman service years. He died from a fall. Four villagers died weeks later and named him. The exhumation found no decay and fresh blood at the mouth. Europe's newspapers carried the word vampire that year. Case File II covers Petar Blagojević. Save the series: alloccult.com

reels.title: The Demon Catalogue
reels.hook: He listed demons to save accused witches

beats.text: Johann Weyer. Court physician to Wilhelm, Duke of Cleves.
1563: De praestigiis daemonum. Most accused witches were sick, not guilty.
Jean Bodin answered in 1580. He demanded the fire.
1577: Weyer appended a catalogue. Sixty-nine demons, ranked by legions.
He printed it to expose the conjurers' folly.
The conjurers kept it. The Goetia lists seventy-two.

reels.caption: Johann Weyer defended accused witches in 1563. Many, he wrote in De praestigiis daemonum, were ill or deceived — not guilty of congress with devils. Jean Bodin answered him in 1580, calling Weyer a sorcerer and demanding the fire for witches. Weyer's 1577 edition carried an appendix: Pseudomonarchia Daemonum. Sixty-nine spirits, catalogued to expose the folly of conjurers. Instead, it became a primary source for the Goetia of Solomon, which lists seventy-two. The full lineage is at alloccult.com

reels.title: The Alphabet of Honorius
reels.hook: No one knows who invented this alphabet

beats.text: The Theban script. First printed in 1518 by Johannes Trithemius.
He credited Honorius of Thebes. Through Pietro d'Abano. Proof: none.
Agrippa printed it in 1533. De Occulta Philosophia, Book III.
Twentieth-century witchcraft adopted it as its own sacred cipher.
Which word would you write in it? Answer below.

reels.caption: The Theban alphabet appeared in print in 1518, in Trithemius's Polygraphia. He attributed it to one Honorius of Thebes, transmitted through Pietro d'Abano. No manuscript evidence confirms Honorius wrote a word of it. Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa carried it into De Occulta Philosophia in 1533. Modern witchcraft adopted it as a sacred cipher. Which word would you write in it? Answer below. Every magical alphabet: alloccult.com

reels.title: The Silver Cord
reels.hook: Would you leave your body tonight

beats.text: Ecclesiastes 12:6: "Or ever the silver cord be loosed…"
Occultists read that line as a tether. Body to soul.
1929. Muldoon and Carrington publish The Projection of the Astral Body.
Muldoon claimed his first exit at twelve, in a Spiritualist camp.
If the cord held, would you go? Answer below. ☽

reels.caption: "Or ever the silver cord be loosed…" — Ecclesiastes 12:6. Occultists read a tether between the body and the soul. In 1929, Sylvan Muldoon and Hereward Carrington mapped the mechanics of exit in The Projection of the Astral Body. Muldoon claimed his first projection at twelve, waking in a Spiritualist camp unable to control his phantom limbs. He spent a decade refining the method. If the cord held — if the return was guaranteed — would you go? Yes or no, below. The full entry: alloccult.com ☽
